concepts.title: The Witness Clause
concepts.premise: A truth-scribe whose sworn records become law, and whose every oath costs a word of her mother tongue, is bound within a hundred paces of the border-lord on trial for burning his own villages. The forged record that condemns him is in her own hand.
concepts.world_rule: Oath-Law: sworn records are binding fact; each oath erases a word of the scribe's mother tongue

originality.note: Without Oath-Law there's no binding, cost or forgery
Is truth worth more than mercy?
Get evidence to his surviving villagers
The institution of the record is the problem
Record over people → testimony over record
Inverts who holds power; honours slow-burn HEA
A court scribe whose oaths become law falls for the lord on trial
Promising is a legal act

concepts.title: Debt of Warmth
concepts.premise: In a frozen city where heat is money passed by touch, a debt auditor is trapped by a killing frost with the smuggler who gives warmth away, and learns that honest, consenting touch creates heat from nothing.
concepts.world_rule: Warmth Economy: heat moves by touch, never created, except consenting contact between two fully honest people makes surplus

originality.note: Without the Warmth Economy, touch has no cost or surplus
Is a world of debts fairer than a world of gifts?
Find the coal buyer; keep the hearths alive
An economic system, not a villain
Everything is owed → accepting a gift
Inverts institutional power; honours forced proximity
A frozen city where heat is currency passed by touch
Touch and honesty are economic acts

concepts.title: A Name Held in Trust
concepts.premise: An envoy from a conquered river province marries the empire's Warden-General and is given his true name, total command over him. Her people sent her to use it. He knows, and gives it to her anyway.
concepts.world_rule: Name-Ownership: a held true name commands without refusal; each command scars the speaker's voice; names can be split, merging the holders

originality.note: Without Name-Ownership there's no gift of power or dilemma
Is trust real if betrayal is impossible?
His mutiny in the war council
Killing the Emperor doesn't free the names
Love is leverage → a gift never spent
Inverts arranged-marriage power; honours the slow burn
She's given her husband's true name and sent to use it
Naming is an act of state
